events.title: Borland Delphi 1.0 launched
events.summary: Borland launched Delphi 1.0 on February 14, 1995 at Software Development West — a visual Pascal IDE with native Windows GUI compilation.
events.about: Delphi combined Object Pascal with a drag-and-drop form designer and fast native x86 code — the go-to tool for Windows desktop apps in the 1990s. Database grids, reporting tools, and line-of-business software shipped by the thousands. Anders Hejlsberg's team later moved to Microsoft and shaped C#.

narrative.whyChosen: Delphi proved rapid application development could compile to fast native Windows binaries, not just interpreted BASIC.
narrative.whyImportant: It kept Pascal relevant for a decade of GUI development and influenced later RAD tools and C#.
narrative.problemSolved: Windows developers wanted Visual Basic ease with C++-class performance and a real component model.
